title: Courgette and lime cake
subtitle: a moist all-in-one cake with grated courgette and a sharp lime drizzle
excerpt: Grated courgette dissolves into the batter during baking, leaving no vegetable flavour but contributing exceptional moisture. The lime zest in the batter and a lime juice drizzle on top give a sharp, fragrant finish. The cake is made by the all-in-one method and takes under two hours from start to finish.
sourceNotes: Courgette cake is a British home-baking recipe popular from the early 2000s, analogous to the American courgette bread tradition. Lime variation from contemporary British patisserie.

glossaryTerms.definition: Grated courgette adds moisture to a cake batter without flavour. The courgette cell walls collapse during baking, releasing water that keeps the crumb moist for longer than a standard butter cake.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze un-drizzled, wrapped tightly in cling film. Defrost at room temperature and drizzle before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 4 days. The texture improves on day 2.

content.text: contributes moisture, not flavour. Do not squeeze the grated courgette dry before adding it: the water it releases during baking is what keeps the cake moist. Use courgettes that are firm and not oversized; very large courgettes have a watery, hollow centre with little body.

items.prepNote: zest only for batter; keep juice for drizzle

content.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Grease a 900 g loaf tin and line with baking parchment.
In a large bowl, whisk together the vegetable oil, caster sugar, and eggs until well combined. Stir in the lime zest.
Fold in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and cinnamon until just combined, then fold in the grated courgette. The batter will be thick.
Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean and the top is golden and springs back when pressed.

While the cake is in the oven, mix the lime juice and granulated sugar together. As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, prick the top all over with a skewer and spoon the drizzle over slowly. Leave to cool in the tin for 20 minutes before turning out.

attrs.problem: Cake very dense and barely risen
attrs.avoid: Avoid squeezing out the courgette; the water is part of the recipe's hydration.
attrs.fix: Check that the bicarbonate of soda is fresh; stale raising agents will not give a rise.

attrs.problem: Green strands of courgette visible in the finished cake
attrs.avoid: Avoid grating courgette too coarsely; fine strands disappear more fully during baking.
attrs.fix: Use the fine side of a box grater for future batches. Green strands do not affect flavour or texture.
